The Odisha Public Service Commission (OPSC) declared the OCS Prelims Result 2026 on 10 July 2026. The result covers candidates who appeared in the Odisha Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2025, held under Advertisement No. 05 of 2025-26. Below is a quick snapshot of the key facts.

OPSC OCS Prelims Result 2026 - Overview

Particular Details
Conducting Body Odisha Public Service Commission (OPSC)
Exam Name Odisha Civil Services (OCS) Preliminary Examination 2025
Advertisement Number 05 of 2025-26
Prelims Exam Date 7 June 2026
Result Declared On 10 July 2026
Total Candidates Qualified for Mains 5,690 (including 1,905 women candidates)
Notified Vacancies 465 (Group A and Group B posts)
Next Stage OCS Main (Written) Examination 2025 - tentatively October 2026
Result Format Roll number-wise PDF (screening list, not a merit list with marks)
Official Website opsc.gov.in

Important Dates

  • Preliminary Examination held: 7 June 2026
  • Prelims Result declared: 10 July 2026
  • OCS Main (Written) Examination: Tentatively October 2026 (exact schedule not yet notified)

OPSC OCS Prelims Result 2026: Key Highlights

As per the official notice released by OPSC on 10 July 2026, a total of 5,690 candidates, including 1,905 women candidates, have been provisionally shortlisted for the OCS Main Written Examination. The Preliminary Examination was conducted on 7 June 2026 for recruitment to various Group A and Group B posts under the Odisha Civil Services.

Vacancy Details

The Odisha Civil Services (Combined) Preliminary Examination 2025 was conducted against 465 vacancies spread across various Group A and Group B posts under the Odisha Civil Services. A post-wise vacancy breakdown was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article; candidates should refer to the original recruitment notification (Advt. No. 05 of 2025-26) on opsc.gov.in for the exact post-wise distribution.

How to Download OPSC OCS Prelims Result 2026 PDF

  1. Visit the official OPSC website: opsc.gov.in
  2. Go to the "What's New" or "Results" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the link titled "OCS Prelims Result 2026" or "Odisha Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2025 - Result."
  4. The result will open as a PDF file containing a roll number-wise list.
  5. Press Ctrl + F (Windows) or Cmd + F (Mac) to open the search box.
  6. Type your roll number and press Enter to check your status.
  7. Download and save the PDF for future reference, especially for the Mains application process.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Verify your roll number carefully in the PDF using Ctrl+F.
  • Save/download the result PDF for future reference.
  • Regularly check opsc.gov.in for the Mains exam schedule and admit card updates.
  • In case of any discrepancy in the result, contact the Commission through the official channels mentioned on the OPSC website.
  • Qualifying the Prelims is provisional; final eligibility is subject to document verification at later stages.

Important Links

  • Official Website:opsc.gov.in
  • Direct Link: OPSC OCS Prelims Result 2026

The Gujarat Public Service Commission (GPSC) has issued a revised final result notification dated 05-08-2026 for the posts of Deputy Section Officer, Class-III and Deputy Mamlatdar, Class-III under the Special Recruitment Drive for Persons with Disabilities (Advertisement No. 127/2024-25). The notification number is APE-127/2024-25-Main-CNF (Revised), signed by Joint Secretary Dharmendrasinh Chauhan at Gandhinagar.

Direct Link to Check GPSC Deputy Section Officer & Deputy Mamlatdar Revised Result 2026

GPSC Deputy Section Officer and Deputy Mamlatdar Result 2026 - Quick Overview

Detail Information
Notification Number APE-127/2024-25-Main-CNF (Revised)
Notification Date 05-08-2026
Advertisement Number 127/2024-25
Posts Covered Deputy Section Officer, Class-III and Deputy Mamlatdar, Class-III (Special Recruitment Drive for Persons with Disabilities)
Conducting Body Gujarat Public Service Commission (GPSC)
Main Examination Dates 20 to 22 February 2026
Previous Result (Cancelled) 16-07-2026, cancelled ab initio
Total Successful Candidates Listed 63
Applicable Rules Deputy Section Officer, Class-III and Deputy Mamlatdar, Class-III Combined Competitive Examination Rules, 2018 (as amended)

Why Was the Result Revised?

According to the notification, GPSC received representations from candidates about their disability percentage after the earlier result was declared. On review, the Commission found discrepancies between the disability percentage entered by candidates at the time of application and the percentage mentioned in the medical certificate produced during document verification after the preliminary test. In the larger interest of candidates, the Commission cancelled the 16-07-2026 result ab initio and provisionally published this revised result.

Also Read: RSSB Informatics Assistant 2023 Final Result

Important Dates

Event Date
Main Examination (Paper 1 & Paper 2 – Gujarati and English) 20 to 22 February 2026
Common Paper Self-Declaration Notice Published 10-02-2026
Original Final Result (Cancelled) 16-07-2026
Revised Result Notification 05-08-2026

Category-Wise Revised Cut-Off Marks

The cut-off mark for each PwD category is the score obtained by the last candidate in the merit list of that respective benchmark disability group, as arranged in descending order of total marks.

Group Cut-Off Marks (Revised)
Group A 158.10
Group B 119.80
Group C 169.55
Group D (d & e) 58.40

Marking Scheme for Language Papers

Evaluation of Paper-1 (Gujarati Language) and Paper-2 (English Language) has been carried out using the Final Answer Key, awarding 1.000 mark for each correct answer and deducting 0.300 mark for each wrong answer, multiple-encoded answer, or blank answer.

Common Paper Adjustment for Overlapping Advertisements

The main examination for Paper-1 (Gujarati) and Paper-2 (English) under Advertisement Numbers 67, 127/2024-25, and 08/2025-26 was conducted together on 22-02-2026. Candidates who had registered in more than one of these advertisements were given a self-declaration link, published via a notice dated 10-02-2026, to indicate which advertisement's common paper marks should be considered. Based on the details submitted, the relevant common paper marks have accordingly been applied across these advertisements.

Also Read: CSU Non Teaching Admit Card 2026

Legal Status – Gujarat High Court Case

The Commission has clarified that this entire result is subject to the final decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat in Special Civil Application (SCA) No. 7858/2026.

The full merit list contains 63 successful candidates. A sample of the top entries from Annexure-I (Part-I) is given below; candidates should refer to the official PDF for the complete list.

4 108002562 Ms. Maheshwariba Bhupatsinh Jadeja C 202.75 C-2

Note: The complete list of 63 successful candidates and 148 unsuccessful candidates, along with their category, gender, birth date, PwD group, disability percentage, sports/widow status, and post preference order, is published in Annexure-I (Part-I and Part-II) of the official PDF notification.

Required Documents

This information is not available in the official notification. The document is a result notification, not a recruitment advertisement, and does not list documents required for the next stage of appointment.

How to Apply / Next Steps

This information is not available in the official notification, since no application process is described here. This is a result declaration, not an application notice. Candidates should watch the Commission's official website for further communication regarding document verification, medical examination outcomes, and appointment procedures.

Important Instructions

Success in the examination does not confer any right to appointment. No candidate will be appointed to the post unless the Government, after any inquiries it considers necessary, is satisfied that the candidate is suitable in all respects for the post. The above result is subject to revision after rechecking of marks for those candidates who apply for rechecking. Candidates are advised to visit the Commission's website for further instructions and guidelines.

Both were published on the official RSSB results page. Candidates who appeared for this recruitment and completed document verification should check both PDFs to confirm their selection status.

What Do These Two Documents Mean?

Both documents relate to candidates who have already gone through document verification (DV) for the Informatics Assistant 2023 recruitment:

  • Order of Final Recommendation after DV (List No. 05): This is an official order recommending a further batch of candidates for appointment, following completion of their document verification. The "List No. 05" label indicates this is the fifth such recommendation list issued for this recruitment details of Lists 01 to 04, if any, are Not Available Officially on this page.
  • Meritwise List of Finally Selected Candidates after DV: This is the merit-ordered list of candidates who have been finally selected after their documents were verified.

How to Check Your Name in the RSSB Informatics Assistant List

  1. Visit the official RSSB results page at rssb.rajasthan.gov.in/results.
  2. Look for the entries dated 06-08-2026 under "Informatics Assistant 2023."
  3. Click the download icon next to "Order of Final Recommendation after DV (List no-05)" or "Meritwise List of Finally Selected Candidates after DV," as needed.
  4. Open the PDF and use Ctrl+F (or the search function on mobile) to look for your roll number or name.
  5. Save or print the page confirming your status for future reference.

Also Read: RRB Group D City Intimation Slip 2026

Important Instructions

  • Both lists are specific to candidates who have already undergone document verification for Informatics Assistant 2023 this is not a fresh notification or a new vacancy announcement.
  • If your roll number does not appear in either list, RSSB has not specified next steps in the source used for this article; candidates in this situation are advised to check the official notice or contact RSSB directly. This is Not Available Officially here.
  • Any joining instructions, posting orders, or further document requirements tied to this list are Not Available Officially refer to the official PDF and any accompanying office order for details.
  • Always cross-check your roll number and personal details carefully against the official PDF; do not rely solely on third-party result-checking sites.

The result covers candidates who appeared for Level 1 (PRT), Level 2 (TGT), and Level 3 (PGT) in the exam conducted on 4-5 July 2026. HTET Result 2026: Qualifying Marks

BSEH has kept the HTET qualifying marks consistent for several years, applying the same category-wise pattern to the 2026 result cycle:

Category Qualifying Marks (out of 150) Percentage
General 90 60%
SC / OBC / PwD (Haryana Domicile) 82 ~55%

This qualifying pattern is based on BSEH's established practice from previous HTET cycles, as reported consistently across exam-news portals. It was not restated as a separate figure in the 5 August 2026 result notice reviewed for this article, so candidates should confirm the exact 2026 qualifying marks against the official scorecard or the final answer key notice on bseh.org.in.

How to Check and Download HTET Result 2026

  1. Visit the official BSEH HTET result portal.
  2. Click on the "HTET Result 2026" link for your level (PRT / TGT / PGT).
  3. Enter your enrollment number or registration number, along with your date of birth.
  4. Submit the details to view your scorecard on screen.
  5. Check your marks, qualifying status, and category.
  6. Download and save the result PDF.
  7. Take a printout for future reference and certificate applications.

Documents Required to Check HTET Result 2026

  • HTET Enrollment Number or Registration Number
  • Date of Birth (as per application form)
  • Admit Card (for reference, as roll number and login details are printed on it)

HTET 2026 Disqualified Candidate List and Biometric Verification

Along with the scorecard link, BSEH has also released a disqualified/cancelled candidate list and a list of candidates whose biometric verification is pending. Candidates whose names appear in either list should check the official notice PDF for the specific reason and next steps, since this is not detailed in the result link itself.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Use the same enrollment number and date of birth that were used during the application/admit card stage.
  • Cross-check your name, father's name, category, and level on the scorecard; report discrepancies to BSEH through the official channel.
  • Save a digital copy and a printed copy of the result it is required later for the HTET eligibility certificate and for recruitment applications.
  • Only candidates who meet the qualifying marks for their category receive the HTET eligibility certificate.
  • Keep checking bseh.org.in for the certificate download link, which is typically issued after the result.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC) released the hall ticket for the Combined Technical Services Examination (Non-Interview Posts) on 6 August 2026, under Advertisement No. 734, Notification No. 04/2026. The written examination is scheduled to be held across multiple subject-wise sessions from 16 August 2026 to 19 September 2026. This article covers the download process, exam schedule, and exam-day requirements for this recruitment cycle.

Direct Link to Download TNPSC CTS Non-Interview Hall Ticket 2026

TNPSC CTS Non-Interview Hall Ticket 2026 - Quick Overview

Detail Information
Organisation Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC)
Examination Combined Technical Services Examination (Non-Interview Posts)
Advertisement No. / Notification No. 734 / 04/2026
Hall Ticket Release Date 6 August 2026
Exam Dates 16 August 2026 to 19 September 2026 (revised schedule per Addendum 4B/2026)
Exam Mode Written Examination (Single Stage), subject-wise sessions
Official Websites tnpsc.gov.in and tnpscexams.in
Login Credentials Required Registration/OTR ID or Application ID + Date of Birth

TNPSC CTS Non-Interview 2026 Important Dates

Event Date
Notification Release 20 May 2026
Online Application Start Date 27 May 2026
Last Date to Apply Online 25 June 2026 (11:59 PM)
Application Correction Window 29 June 2026 to 1 July 2026
Addendum Adding Vacancies 11 June 2026 and 16 July 2026 (Addendum 4B)
Hall Ticket Release Date 6 August 2026
Examination Dates 16 August 2026 to 19 September 2026

TNPSC CTS Non-Interview Vacancy Details

This recruitment covers non-interview technical and professional posts such as Assistant Engineer, Assistant Geologist, Agriculture Officer, Drug Inspector, Horticultural Officer, Junior Scientific Officer, and Block Health Statistician, among others, across various Tamil Nadu government departments and public sector organisations.

  • 476 vacancies across 45 posts at original notification (20 May 2026)
  • 16 additional vacancies added via addendum on 11 June 2026
  • 32 additional vacancies added via Addendum 4B/2026 on 16 July 2026, with two posts (Assistant Engineer – Mechanical, and Junior Chemist) reported as withdrawn in the same addendum
  • Total figures reported by different sources after these revisions range from 508 to 524; one source separately reports 461

How to Download TNPSC CTS Non-Interview Hall Ticket 2026

  1. Visit the official website, tnpsc.gov.in (or tnpscexams.in).
  2. Click on the "Hall Ticket Download" link under the Important Links / Announcements section.
  3. Select the link for Combined Technical Services Examination (Non-Interview Posts), Notification No. 04/2026.
  4. Enter your Registration Number / OTR ID / Application ID and Date of Birth.
  5. Complete the captcha verification, if prompted.
  6. Click Submit to view the hall ticket on screen.
  7. Verify all printed details carefully, then download and print the admit card in A4 size.

Details Mentioned on the Hall Ticket

  • Candidate's name, photograph, and signature
  • Registration number and roll number
  • Exam name, subject/paper details
  • Exam date and session/shift
  • Examination centre name, address, and reporting time
  • Exam-day instructions

Per TNPSC's own instructions for this cycle, the exam centre allotted is final as printed on the hall ticket the Commission does not permit change-of-centre requests after allotment, though it reserves the right to increase, decrease, or re-allot centres itself.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • A printed copy of the TNPSC CTS Hall Ticket 2026, in A4 size, with print margins not exceeding 5 mm top and bottom (per TNPSC's stated print guidance)
  • One valid original photo ID proof Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, Passport, Driving Licence, or PAN Card
  • A recent passport-size photograph matching the one uploaded during application, where specified on the hall ticket

Also Read: SSC JHT PST 2026 Date

Important Instructions for Exam Day

  • Reach the exam centre well before the reporting time printed on the hall ticket; late entry is not permitted under any circumstances.
  • Carry only the required documents electronic devices and other prohibited items are not permitted inside the exam hall.
  • Follow all instructions issued by TNPSC to avoid disqualification.
  • Do not leave the examination hall before the session ends.
  • Report any discrepancy in hall ticket details to TNPSC immediately, rather than waiting until exam day.

Selection Process

The selection process for this recruitment comprises: Written Examination (Single Stage), Onscreen Certificate Verification, Physical Certificate Verification and Counselling (wherever applicable), and Final Selection and Ranking based on merit.

Details Mentioned on the MahaJyoti Hall Ticket 2026

Candidates must verify every detail on the admit card immediately after downloading it. The hall ticket generally includes:

  • Candidate name
  • Roll number
  • Application number
  • Exam category and shift
  • Exam date and timing
  • Reporting time
  • Exam centre name, code, and full address
  • Candidate photograph and signature
  • Important instructions for exam day

Documents to Carry Along with MahaJyoti Hall Ticket

Candidates must bring a printed copy of the admit card along with a valid original photo ID proof. Without these, entry to the exam centre may be denied. Accepted ID proofs generally include:

  • Aadhaar Card
  • PAN Card
  • Voter ID Card
  • Driving License
  • Passport

Also Read: JKSSB Staff Nurse Result 2026

Important Instructions for MahaJyoti Candidates

  • Use the correct Aadhaar Number and Mobile Number to log in; repeated incorrect attempts may temporarily lock the account.
  • Download the admit card well ahead of the exam date to avoid last-minute server or technical issues.
  • Carefully verify name, photograph, exam centre, exam date, and shift timing as soon as the hall ticket is downloaded.
  • Ensure details on the admit card match your ID proof exactly, or entry may be refused at the centre.
  • Print the hall ticket clearly on A4-size paper blurred or damaged printouts may not be accepted.
  • Retain the admit card safely even after the exam, for future reference or verification.

What to Do If There Is an Error in Your MahaJyoti Admit Card

If any detail on the hall ticket is incorrect, candidates should report it immediately through the official MahaJyoti website rather than waiting until exam day. Common errors to check for include:

  • Spelling error in candidate name
  • Wrong or unclear photograph
  • Incorrect application number
  • Wrong date of birth
  • Incorrect exam category or shift
  • Wrong exam centre or city
  • Incorrect exam date or time

How to Download CSU Non-Teaching Admit Card 2026

CBI Apprentice Vacancy Details 2026

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Admit Card 2026 - Released

The RBI Grade B Phase 1 call letter was released on 5th June 2026, ahead of the Phase 1 examination held on 13th June 2026. The call letter was made available through the official RBI recruitment portal and candidates were required to log in with their registration credentials to access it. This section also applies to candidates of DEPR and DSIM posts, whose Phase 1 exam was scheduled for 14th June 2026.

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

RBI Grade B Mains Admit Card 2026 - Expected in July

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. RBI typically releases the Mains hall ticket approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date, so candidates should watch the official website closely during the second week of July.

The Mains exam is a comprehensive paper that tests a candidate's knowledge of Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, and English Writing Skills. Unlike Phase 1, Phase 2 marks are directly counted in the final selection.

 

How to Download RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026

Downloading the RBI Grade B call letter is a straightforward process. The same steps apply for both Phase 1 (already released) and Phase 2 (upcoming). Follow the steps below to access your hall ticket from the official website.

Step 1: Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at https://opportunities.rbi.org.in/

Step 2: Look for the admit card link under the "Call Letter" section select the link for the relevant phase (Phase 1 or Phase 2).

Step 3: A login page will appear on your screen.

Step 4: Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth / Password in the respective fields.

Step 5: Click on the Submit button. Your RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 will be displayed on the screen.

Step 6: Carefully verify all the details printed on the call letter name, roll number, exam centre, and shift timing.

Step 7: Download and take at least 2 printouts to carry on exam day.

Step 8: Read all exam day instructions mentioned on the call letter before the examination.

Details to Verify on Your RBI Grade B Call Letter

After downloading the admit card, candidates must cross-check the following details to ensure everything is accurate. If any discrepancy is found, it must be reported to RBI's recruitment authorities immediately.

The call letter will contain the following information:

Candidate's Name, Roll Number and Registration Number, Photograph and Signature, Date of Birth, Category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PwBD), Post Applied For, Exam Date and Shift Timing, Reporting Time and Gate Closing Time, Exam Centre Name, Address, and Code, and Important Exam Day Instructions.

Documents to Carry to the RBI Grade B Exam Centre

Carrying the right documents to the examination centre is mandatory. Entry will not be granted if the candidate fails to produce valid identity proof along with the printed admit card.

Every candidate must bring the following on exam day:

Printed copy of the RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026, 2 recent passport-size photographs, one valid original Photo ID proof such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence, and a photocopy of the same Photo ID.

PwBD candidates should additionally refer to the Instructions for PwBD Candidates using Scribe and/or Compensatory Time document available on the official website.

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Shift Timing 2026

The Phase 1 exam for General posts was conducted on 13th June 2026 in a single shift. Candidates were required to arrive at the exam centre well before the gate closing time. The general shift schedule for the exam is outlined below.

Exam Phase Reporting Time Gate Closing Time Exam Time
Phase 1 1:00 PM 1:45 PM 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM

Note: Individual admit cards may contain slightly different timings based on centre and shift allocation. Always follow the timing printed on your specific call letter.

RBI Grade B Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Section Questions Marks Duration
Reasoning Ability 60 60 45 Minutes
English Language 30 30 25 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 30 25 Minutes
General Knowledge (GA) 80 80 25 Minutes
Total 200 200 120 Minutes

Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Pattern - Objective + Descriptive

Phase 2 is the main scoring round with 300 marks spread across 3 papers. Both objective and descriptive components are tested. Marks from this stage directly determine the final merit list.

Paper Subject Question Type Marks Duration
Paper I Economic & Social Issues (ESI) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes
Paper III Finance & Management (FM) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Total     300 330 Minutes

RBI Grade B Exam Day Instructions 2026

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. Electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and books are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. The exam centre and date allotted on the call letter are final no requests for change of centre, date, or session will be entertained.

Educational Qualification

Candidates applying for the post of Village Accountant must have passed PUC (Pre-University Course, equivalent to Class 12) or a qualification recognized as equivalent to PUC by the Government of Karnataka. Equivalent qualifications include:

  • Class 12 examination conducted by CBSE or ICSE boards.

  • Advanced vocational courses/NSDC-affiliated courses conducted through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS).

  • Candidates who completed a three-year diploma from a technical education department institution before 2015 are also required to have cleared the Kannada-language subject through an SSLC-level examination.

  • Persons already serving in Karnataka Government, local body, State/Central statutory or PSU service - relaxation equal to years of service or 10 years, whichever is less.
  • Ex-servicemen - relaxation equal to the length of service rendered, plus 3 years.
  • National Cadet Corps (NCC) full-time supervisors - relaxation equal to years of service.
  • Persons employed as Grama Samuha Parishilakaru under the rural self-employment scheme - relaxation equal to years of service.
  • Special Chetana (persons with disabilities) candidates - 10 years relaxation.
  • Persons employed by the Government of India census organization in Karnataka - relaxation equal to years of service or 5 years, whichever is less.
  • Widows who have not remarried, or women legally divorced and not remarried - 10 years relaxation, subject to proof.
  • Retrenched employees who repaid retrenchment compensation as per the Karnataka Retrenched Employees Act/1957 rules - 10 years relaxation, subject to proof.
  • Transgender/third-gender candidates - 1% horizontal reservation with corresponding age relaxation as per the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

KEA VAO Selection Process 2026

Selection to the post of Village Accountant is made purely through a competitive written examination; the notification does not mention any separate interview round. The process is as follows:

  • Candidates will appear for a competitive written examination conducted in Offline-OMR mode.
  • A minimum of 35% marks in the competitive exam is required for eligibility; candidates scoring below this will be disqualified.
  • Candidates opting for the Kannada language exam exemption must have passed Kannada as first or second language up to SSLC level, or must clear a compulsory qualifying Kannada language test (150 marks, minimum 50 marks required to qualify). This paper is not counted toward merit ranking.
  • District-wise merit lists / marks lists will be prepared and forwarded by KEA to the respective District Magistrates for appointment, which is made at the district level.

KEA VAO Exam Pattern 2026

The written examination consists of two papers, each carrying 100 marks and lasting 2 hours, with negative marking of 0.25 marks for every wrong answer.

Paper Subject Total Questions Total Marks Duration
Paper 1 General Knowledge (current affairs, general science, Indian Constitution, Indian and Karnataka history and geography, Panchayat Raj and rural cooperative institutions, and Karnataka regional issues and development) 100 100 2 hours
Paper 2 General Kannada, General English, and Computer Knowledge 100 100 2 hours

Each question offers 4 answer options with only one correct answer. A minimum qualifying score of 35% is required in the competitive exam.

How to Apply for KEA VAO Recruitment 2026

Applicants must apply strictly online through the KEA CET portal by following the steps below.

  1. Visit the official KEA website: cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea
  2. Click on the application link for VAO Recruitment 2026 applicable to your cadre (General/RPC or Kalyana-Karnataka).
  3. Register with your basic details and generate login credentials.
  4. Fill in the online application form with personal, educational, and category details, selecting only one district of preference.
  5. Upload a recent passport-size photograph (JPEG format, 50KB-200KB) and signature (JPEG format, 50KB-70KB) as per the specified format.
  6. Verify all entered details carefully, as no correction is allowed after submission.
  7. Pay the applicable application fee online and complete the submission.
  8. Download and retain a printout of the submitted application and fee payment receipt for future reference.

KEA VAO Important Instructions

  • Applications will be accepted online only; offline or postal applications will not be considered.
  • Candidates can apply to only one district; applications submitted for more than one district will not be accepted.
  • Original documents must be produced at the time of document verification for eligibility, age, and category claims. Failure to appear with valid original documents on the specified date will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Candidates are responsible for reading all eligibility instructions before applying; incomplete or incorrect information may result in rejection of candidature at any stage.
  • Impersonation, submission of forged documents, or use of unfair means during the exam or interview process will lead to disqualification and possible criminal/disciplinary action.
  • Aadhaar Card is mandatory for application submission.

CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL), Bengaluru, a unit under the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, has released Advertisement No. 13/2026/PS (published 05.08.2026) inviting applications for engagement of Project Staff - Project Assistant (PA-I, PA-II), Project Associate (PAT-I, PAT-I NET/GATE, PAT-II, PAT-II NET/GATE), Senior PAT, and Principal PAT - to work on CSIR, externally-funded, and other projects at CSIR-NAL. CSIR-NAL Recruitment 2026 has no online application - candidates must attend the Walk-in-Interview in person between 10 and 25 August 2026, on the specific date assigned to the post and specialization they are applying for.

Quick answers: CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL), Bengaluru is recruiting Project Staff across roughly 14 post/specialization combinations spanning Aerospace, Mechanical, Electronics, Chemistry, Metallurgy, and Computer Science disciplines. Adding the position-wise numbers gives approximately 89 posts (computed; the notification does not state one combined total). Only Indian Nationals who already hold the required degree/diploma (no result-awaited candidates) can apply, with age limit 35 years for all posts. There is no apply-online step and no application fee - candidates must walk in with the prescribed application form and documents. Walk-in-Interviews run from 10 August 2026 to 25 August 2026, at CSIR-NAL (RAB Meeting Complex), Kodihalli, Bengaluru – 560017, with registration from 9:00 AM to 9:45 AM on each interview date.

CSIR-NAL Eligibility Criteria & Qualification 2026

Eligibility depends on the post level and the specialization applied for. General essential qualification for each post category is summarized below; the exact discipline (e.g. Mechanical, Electronics, Chemistry) must match the specialization listed in the Vacancy table for the post code applied to.

CSIR-NAL Selection Process 2026

Selection is based on performance in the interview, or any other criteria adopted by the Selection Committee. If a large number of candidates appear, the Selection/Screening Committee has the discretion to shortlist candidates through a written exam or any other criteria it deems fit before the interview. A panel of suitable candidates is drawn up after the selection process, valid for a maximum of one year; empanelment does not automatically guarantee engagement, and utilization depends on the number of positions available across projects during that period.

How to Apply for CSIR-NAL Recruitment 2026 (Walk-in-Interview Process)

CSIR-NAL Recruitment 2026 has no apply-online option, and applications sent by post, speed post, or e-mail are explicitly not accepted.

  1. Download the prescribed Application Form for Walk-in-Interview (Advt. No. 13/2026/PS) from the CSIR-NAL website and fill it completely.
  2. Report in person at CSIR-NAL (RAB Meeting Complex, National Aerospace Laboratories), Adjacent to SBI NAL Branch, Kodihalli, Bengaluru – 560017, between 9:00 AM and 9:45 AM on the date fixed for the post/specialization you are applying for.
  3. Bring a copy of your Aadhaar Card or another Government-issued photo ID, the duly filled application form, a latest passport-size photograph, and original certificates along with one set of photocopies (including Caste Certificate, if applicable, in the proper format).
  4. Candidates wishing to apply for more than one position must apply separately for each position.
  5. Be prepared to return the next day if your interview is not completed on the scheduled date for any reason.

No TA/DA is paid for attending the Walk-in-Interview. Candidates already working in CSIR-NAL or any other CSIR lab must bring a "No Objection Certificate" from their Project Leader/HOD at the time of interview.

Indian Army JAG Entry Scheme 125th Course Selection Process

  1. Application submission and shortlisting (based on CLAT PG 2026 score and vacancy-to-call-up ratio).
  2. Selection of SSB Centre and Date (first-come-first-served, once selected cannot be changed by the candidate).
  3. SSB Interview (two-stage selection at Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bengaluru, or Jalandhar) - duration up to five days. Candidates failing Stage-I are returned the same day.
  4. Medical Examination for candidates recommended after Stage-II.
  5. Merit List preparation based on SSB marks.
  6. Joining Letter for Pre-Commission Training at OTA, Chennai, subject to eligibility and vacancy.

Qualifying the SSB interview alone does not confirm final selection - final selection depends on the merit list and availability of vacancies.

Documents Required for SSB Interview

  • Signed printout of the online application with self-attested photograph.
  • Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate (or equivalent) and mark sheet.
  • 12th Class Certificate and Mark Sheet.
  • Graduation Degree/Provisional Degree (for three-year LLB after graduation).
  • LLB Degree/Provisional Degree from a recognized university.
  • Mark sheets of all years/semesters.
  • Registration with Bar Council of India/State, or a certificate confirming the LLB course is recognized by the Bar Council of India.
  • University certificate on the CGPA-to-percentage conversion formula (if applicable).
  • CLAT PG 2026 Score Card (conducted in December 2025).

DigiLocker certificates will not be accepted in place of original certificates. All original documents must be carried for verification at the SSB; originals are returned after verification.

Also Read: IAF Agniveervayu Musician Recruitment 2026 (Intake 01/2027) - Apply Online, Eligibility, Dates

How to Apply for Indian Army JAG Entry Scheme 125th Course

  1. Visit www.joinindianarmy.nic.in and click on 'Officer Entry Application/Login'.
  2. Click 'Registration' (not required if already registered on the website).
  3. Fill the online registration form after reading the instructions carefully.
  4. After registration, click 'Apply Online' under the Dashboard.
  5. On the 'Officer Selection – Eligibility' page, click 'Apply' against Short Service Commission JAG Entry Course.
  6. Fill in personal information, communication details, education details, and previous SSB details (if any) under the 'Application Form' page.
  7. Review the summary of information, then click 'Submit' only after confirming all details are correct.
  8. Take two printouts of the application (with roll number) 30 minutes after the online application closes on the last day.

Important Instructions

  • No changes can be made to the online application after it closes; no representation on this will be entertained.
  • CGPA/Grades must be converted to marks as per the university's formula before filling in the application.
  • The candidate's name, parents' names, and date of birth in the profile and application must match the Matriculation/Secondary School certificate exactly.
  • Only one online application per candidate is allowed; multiple applications will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Candidates serving in the Armed Forces must inform their Commanding Officer in writing and carry a countersigned application to the SSB.
  • Requests to change the SSB interview date or centre will not be entertained.
  • Candidates must report within 7 days of their candidature reporting date, or their candidature will be cancelled.
  • Candidates who marry after the date of application, or during training, will lose eligibility or be withdrawn from training.
  • In case of any discrepancy between the English and Hindi versions of the notification, the English version shall prevail.

The Directorate General of Quality Assurance (DGQA), Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, Government of India, has invited applications for Direct Recruitment to 07 Technician (Semi Skilled) and 07 Technician (Skilled) Group 'C', Non-Ministerial, Industrial posts vide Advertisement No. CQA(S)/2026/Tech(SS) & Tech(SK), published in Employment News, 8–14 August 2026. DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 does not use an online application portal - eligible candidates must send a duly filled physical application by Registered or Speed Post to the Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Systems), Secunderabad.

Quick answers: DGQA is recruiting for 14 Technician posts (07 Skilled + 07 Semi Skilled) across six establishment codes in Secunderabad, Bengaluru, Jabalpur, and Chandigarh. Only Indian Nationals aged 18–27 years (as on the application closing date) with Matriculation + ITI/relevant trade qualification can apply. There is no online application; candidates must post their application by Registered/Speed Post. The closing date is 21 days from the date of publication of the advertisement in Employment News (28 days for candidates from specified remote/northeastern regions and island territories). Selection is through a Written Test followed by a Trade Test - there is no interview.

  • DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 Employment News Notification PDF

DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 Overview

Particulars Details
Organization Directorate General of Quality Assurance (DGQA)
Recruiting Authority Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Systems), Secunderabad
Ministry/Department Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, Government of India
Advertisement No. CQA(S)/2026/Tech(SS) & Tech(SK)
Published In Employment News, 8–14 August 2026 issue
Posts Technician (Skilled) and Technician (Semi Skilled), Group 'C', Non-Ministerial, Industrial
Total Vacancies 14 (07 Technician Semi Skilled + 07 Technician Skilled)
Nature of Recruitment Direct Recruitment; two-year probation on selection
Mode of Application Offline - physical application sent by Registered/Speed Post (no online portal)
Mode of Selection Written Test (Objective/MCQ) followed by Trade Test; no interview
Posting Locations Secunderabad (Telangana), Bengaluru (Karnataka), Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), Chandigarh
Application Address Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Systems), DGQA Technical Complex, Manovikas Nagar P.O., Secunderabad – 500009

DGQA Technician Vacancy 2026 – Establishment-Wise Details

The 14 DGQA Technician vacancies are spread across six establishment codes under different Controllerates/Quality Assurance Establishments. Category-wise distribution as per the notification is shown below.

S. No. Post Name (Establishment Code / Location) No. of Posts
1 Technician (Skilled) - SC-009, Secunderabad 4 (UR-3, OBC-1)
2 Technician (Semi Skilled) - BLR-006, Bengaluru 3 (UR-1, OBC-1, ST-1)
3 Technician (Semi Skilled) - BLR-046, Bengaluru 1 (UR-1)
4 Technician (Skilled) - BLR-046, Bengaluru 2 (UR-2)
5 Technician (Semi Skilled) - JBP-011, Jabalpur 1 (UR-1)
6 Technician (Semi Skilled) - CHD-002, Chandigarh 2 (UR-1, OBC-1)
7 Technician (Skilled) - SC-009/1, Secunderabad 1 (UR-1)

Establishment codes correspond to: SC-009 and SC-009/1 – DGQA Complex, Manovikas Nagar PO, Secunderabad; BLR-006 – Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Radar), JC Nagar PO, Bengaluru; BLR-046 – Senior Quality Assurance Establishment (Electronics), S K Garden, Benson Town PO, Bengaluru; JBP-011 – Senior Quality Assurance Establishment (Electronics), Gun Factory PO, Jabalpur; CHD-002 – Senior Quality Assurance Establishment (Elect & Sys), C/o Ordnance Factory, Chandigarh. Selected candidates are appointed on probation for two years and are liable to serve anywhere within India, including field/remote locations, as per organisational requirement.

DGQA Technician Eligibility & Qualification 2026

Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply. The essential qualification differs for the two posts:

Post Essential Qualification
Technician (Skilled) (i) Matriculation (10th class pass) from a recognized Board or equivalent; AND (ii) ITI Pass Certificate in the specified trade, or an equivalent Defence Services Tradesman Course approved by the Central or State Government; AND one year of experience in the specified trade from a recognized organization or undertaking
Technician (Semi Skilled) ITI pass in any Trade, or its equivalent Defence Services Tradesman course approved by the Central or State Government

Candidates possessing any additional qualification, or pursuing one, as on the application closing date must mention it in the application form.

Also read: Indian Army SSC (Tech)-68 Men Recruitment 2026: Notification, Eligibility, Dates, Salary

DGQA Technician Age Limit 2026

Candidates must be between 18 and 27 years of age as on the application closing date. Date of birth must be as per the 10th/Matriculation certificate or a Birth Certificate issued by a competent authority - Aadhaar Card is not accepted as proof of date of birth.

Category Age Relaxation Beyond Upper Limit
SC/ST 5 years (only for vacancies reserved for SC/ST)
OBC 3 years (only for vacancies reserved for OBC)
Ex-Servicemen (Gen/UR) 3 years after deducting military service rendered, from actual age as on closing date
Ex-Servicemen (OBC) 6 years (3+3) after deducting military service rendered
Ex-Servicemen (SC/ST) 8 years (3+5) after deducting military service rendered
Departmental candidates (min. 3 years continuous service) Up to 40 years (UR), up to 43 years (OBC), up to 45 years (SC/ST)

Age relaxation for a reserved category will remain provisional until the appointing authority verifies the supporting documents. SC/ST/EWS/PwBD/Ex-Servicemen candidates must enclose the latest Caste/relevant certificate from a competent authority (District Magistrate and equivalent, Chief/Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, or a Revenue Officer not below Tehsildar rank/Sub-Divisional Officer of the candidate's area). Central Government civilian employees claiming age relaxation must submit a certificate (Annexure-I) from their office confirming at least 3 years of continuous service as on the closing date.

Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

DGQA Technician Salary 2026

Recruited candidates will draw pay as per the 7th CPC Pay Matrix:

  • Technician (Semi Skilled): Pay Matrix Level-1 (Rs. 18,000 – 56,900)
  • Technician (Skilled): Pay Matrix Level-2 (Rs. 19,900 – 63,200)

In addition to basic pay, selected candidates are entitled to Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, Transport Allowance, Children Education Allowance, Leave Travel Concession, medical facilities, CSD facilities, and other allowances/advances as per extant Government of India rules. Recruited candidates will be covered under the National Pension Scheme (NPS)/Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) as applicable.

DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 Important Dates

Event Date
Advertisement Published in Employment News 8 – 14 August 2026 (issue week)
Application Closing Date (general candidates) 21 days from the date of publication of the advertisement in Employment News
Application Closing Date (candidates from Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim, Ladakh Division of J&K, Lahaul & Spiti and Pangi Sub-Division of Chamba District (HP), Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep) 28 days from the date of publication of the advertisement in Employment News
Written Test / Trade Test Date & Venue Not specified in the notification - communicated through the Admit Card

The notification specifies the closing date as a number of days from publication rather than a fixed calendar date; candidates should confirm the exact closing date against the precise Employment News publication date.

DGQA Technician Application Fee 2026

No separate application fee is mentioned in the notification. However, every applicant must submit one self-addressed envelope (size 30cm x 12cm) affixed with a postal stamp of Rs. 55/- along with the application, for despatch of the admit card. The organisation will not be responsible for non-receipt of the admit card due to an incorrect or incomplete address on this envelope.

Also Read: IAF Agniveervayu Recruitment Rally 2026: Intake 01/2027 for Nagaland & Andaman & Nicobar Islands

DGQA Technician Selection Process 2026

Selection is done through a Written Test followed by a Trade Test - there is no interview.

  • Written Test: Objective type, Multiple Choice Questions only; no negative marking for wrong answers; duration 90 minutes; 100 questions for 100 marks.
Part Subject Questions Marks
(i) General Intelligence and Reasoning 25 25
(ii) General Awareness 25 25
(iii) English Language and Comprehension 25 25
(iv) Numerical Aptitude 25 25
- Total 100 100

Question papers for Parts (i), (ii), and (iv) are set in English and Hindi; Part (iii) is in English only. Candidates are shortlisted for the Trade Test based on written test marks and category of reservation. The Trade Test carries 100 marks, with a minimum qualifying mark of 40. The final merit list is prepared post both tests, based on Trade and Establishment. In case of a tie, resolution is by (1) older date of birth ranked higher, then (2) higher marks in Numerical Aptitude, then Reasoning, then General Awareness.

How to Apply for DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026

DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 has no apply-online option. The application must be sent physically by Registered or Speed Post only.

  1. Fill the application in the prescribed format (Appendix 'A'), typed in English on A4 size paper.
  2. Attach the Admit Card in the prescribed format - Appendix 'B' for Technician (Semi Skilled) or Appendix 'C' for Technician (Skilled) - submitted in duplicate.
  3. Affix one self-attested passport-size photo on the application form, and one self-attested photo on each of the two admit card copies (three photos total).
  4. Enclose a self-addressed envelope (30cm x 12cm) affixed with a postal stamp of Rs. 55/- for admit card despatch.
  5. Clearly superscribe the envelope: "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF [Technician (Semi Skilled) / Technician (Skilled)] AND CATEGORY [SC/ST/OBC/UR]".
  6. Candidates already working in Government Service or a Public Sector Undertaking must route their application through proper channel, with a No Objection Certificate from their Head of Office; applications without this NOC are summarily rejected without further communication.
  7. Send the complete application by Registered/Speed Post to: Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Systems), DGQA Technical Complex, Manovikas Nagar P.O., Secunderabad – 500009.

Applications received after the closing date, even due to postal delay, are rejected summarily and no correspondence is entertained.

DGQA Technician Documents Required 2026

  • Duly completed application in prescribed format (Appendix 'A'), signed and dated
  • Admit Card in prescribed format - Appendix 'B' (Semi Skilled) or Appendix 'C' (Skilled), in duplicate
  • Self-attested copies of Educational Qualification / Technical Qualification / Experience certificates
  • Self-attested copy of Date of Birth Certificate
  • Self-attested copy of Caste Certificate (if applicable)
  • Self-attested copy of Aadhaar Card
  • Self-addressed envelope (30cm x 12cm) with Rs. 55/- postal stamp affixed
  • Three recent passport-size photographs (self-attested)
  • No Objection Certificate from Head of Office (only for candidates already in Government Service/PSU)

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

Sarkari Bharat Vacancies by Sector

Sarkari bharat vacancies span several major recruiting sectors. Each sector below links to a dedicated hub page with sector-specific notifications, eligibility criteria, and exam patterns.

Banking Jobs (IBPS, SBI, RBI)

Banking recruitment includes IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI PO, SBI Clerk, RBI Assistant, and NABARD postings. These roles are among the most competitive sarkari bharat jobs, offering strong starting pay and clear promotion tracks. Browse current openings on our Banking Jobs hub.

Railway Jobs (RRB NTPC, ALP, Group D)

Indian Railways is the country's largest single recruiter, with RRB NTPC, Group D, ALP, JE, and Technician posts opening in large batches. Check live Railway vacancies on our Railway Jobs hub.

Defence Jobs (Army, Navy, Air Force)

Defence recruitment covers Indian Army (including Agniveer), Navy, Air Force, BSF, CRPF, CISF, and ITBP postings. See ongoing openings on our Defence Jobs hub.

Teaching Jobs (KVS, NVS, State Boards)

Teaching sarkari jobs include KVS, NVS, DSSSB, and state education board recruitment for TGT, PGT, and PRT posts. Explore current teaching vacancies on our Teaching Jobs hub.

SSC & UPSC Notifications

SSC (CGL, CHSL, MTS, GD) and UPSC (Civil Services, CDS, NDA) notifications remain the most closely tracked central-government exams. Full notification archives are available on our SSC Jobs and UPSC Jobs hubs.

Not every sarkari job requires a degree. Use the qualification and state filters below to sarkari job find openings that actually match your eligibility, instead of scrolling through listings you don't qualify for.

Several high-volume recruiters - including Railways (Group D), SSC (MTS, GD), and state police departments - recruit primarily at the 10th pass and 12th pass level. Browse these openings on our 10th & 12th Pass Jobs page.

Sarkari Job for Graduates & Postgraduates

Graduate and postgraduate-level sarkari jobs include SSC CGL, Bank PO, UPSC Civil Services, and various state PCS exams. See qualification-matched listings on our Graduate Jobs page.

State-Wise Sarkari Bharat Job (Bihar, UP, Tamil Nadu, and more)

State government recruitment is listed separately by state, since eligibility and domicile rules vary. Find your state's current openings via our State Government Jobs directory.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job refers to any government job opportunity across India's central and state departments - including Railways, Banking, SSC, UPSC, Defence, Police, and PSUs - offering job security, fixed pay scales, and pension benefits under government service rules.

How can I get instant Sarkari Job Alert notifications?

You can bookmark this page for daily updates, or subscribe to OnlyJobs's notification service to receive a Sarkari Job Alert as soon as a new central or state vacancy is announced.

Where can I check the latest Bharat Job Result 2026?

All declared results - including written exam results, merit lists, and interview outcomes - are listed in the Results section of this page, updated as soon as departments release official Bharat Job Result notices.

How do I find a Sarkari Job that matches my qualification?

Use the qualification filters on this page to sarkari job find openings suited to 10th pass, 12th pass, diploma, graduate, or postgraduate candidates, sorted by sector and state.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 में आवेदन कैसे करें?

सबसे पहले संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना पढ़ें, पात्रता जांचें, फिर वैध ईमेल और मोबाइल नंबर से रजिस्ट्रेशन करके फॉर्म भरें, दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें और आवेदन शुल्क जमा करें।

Is OnlyJobs reliable for sarkarijob updates?

Yes - OnlyJobs has tracked sarkarijob notifications since 2011, cross-verifying every listing against official department websites before publishing.

What is the difference between a Sarkari Job and a private-sector job?

Sarkari jobs offer government-backed job security, pension (NPS/OPS), fixed working hours, and statutory benefits, while private jobs typically offer market-driven pay with fewer long-term security guarantees.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.
